verses.zh: 罗波安往示剑去；因为以色列人都到了示剑要立他作王。
verses.en: Rehoboam traveled to Shechem, for all Israel had gathered in[NOTE:1] Shechem to make Rehoboam[NOTE:2] king.
notes: Heb “come [to].”
Heb “him”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 尼八的儿子耶罗波安先前躲避所罗门王，逃往埃及，住在那里（他听见这事。）
verses.en: [NOTE:1] When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard the news, he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.[NOTE:2]
notes: Verse 2 is not included in the Old Greek translation. See the note on 11:43.

Heb “and Jeroboam lived in Egypt.” The parallel text in 2 Chr 10:2 reads, “and Jeroboam returned from Egypt.” In a purely consonantal text the forms “and he lived” and “and he returned” are identical (וישׁב).

verses.zh: 以色列人打发人去请他来，他就和以色列会众都来见罗波安，对他说：
verses.en: They sent for him,[NOTE:1] and Jeroboam and the whole Israelite assembly came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
notes: Heb “They sent and called for him.”

verses.zh: 「你父亲使我们负重轭，做苦工，现在求你使我们做的苦工、负的重轭轻松些，我们就事奉你。」
verses.en: “Your father made us work too hard.[NOTE:1] Now if you lighten the demands he made and don’t make us work as hard, we will serve you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “made our yoke burdensome.”

Heb “but you, now, lighten the burdensome work of your father and the heavy yoke which he placed on us, and we will serve you.” In the Hebrew text the prefixed verbal form with vav (וְנַעַבְדֶךָ, [venaʿavdekha] “and we will serve you”) following the imperative (הָקֵל [haqel], “lighten”) indicates purpose (or result). The conditional sentence used in the translation above is an attempt to bring out the logical relationship between these forms.

verses.zh: 罗波安对他们说：「你们暂且去，第三日再来见我。」民就去了。
verses.en: He said to them, “Go away for three days, then return to me.” So the people went away.

verses.zh: 罗波安之父所罗门在世的日子，有侍立在他面前的老年人，罗波安王和他们商议，说：「你们给我出个甚么主意，我好回覆这民。」
verses.en: King Rehoboam consulted with the older advisers who had served[NOTE:1] his father Solomon when he had been alive. He asked them,[NOTE:2] “How do you advise me to answer these people?”
notes: Heb “stood before.”
Heb “saying.”

verses.zh: 老年人对他说：「现在王若服事这民如仆人，用好话回答他们，他们就永远作王的仆人。」
verses.en: They said to him, “Today if you will be a servant to these people and grant their request,[NOTE:1] speaking kind words to them,[NOTE:2] they will be your servants from this time forward.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and serve them and answer them,” understood as “serve them in how you answer them,” hence “grant their request.”
Heb “and speak to them good words.”
Heb “all the days.” The Hebrew phrase contrasts what he is asked to do “today” (literally “the day”) with the benefit for “all the days.”

verses.zh: 王却不用老年人给他出的主意，就和那些与他一同长大、在他面前侍立的少年人商议，
verses.en: But Rehoboam rejected their advice and consulted the young advisers who served him, with whom he had grown up.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “He rejected the advice of the elders which they advised and he consulted the young men with whom he had grown up, who stood before him.” The referent (Rehoboam) of the initial pronoun (“he”) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 说：「这民对我说：『你父亲使我们负重轭，求你使我们轻松些。』你们给我出个甚么主意，我好回覆他们。」
verses.en: He asked them, “How do you advise me[NOTE:1] to respond to these people who said to me, ‘Lessen the demands your father placed on us’?”[NOTE:2]
notes: In the Hebrew text the verb “we will respond” is plural, although it can be understood as an editorial “we.” The ancient versions have the singular here.
Heb “Lighten the yoke which your father placed on us.”

verses.zh: 那同他长大的少年人说：「这民对王说：『你父亲使我们负重轭，求你使我们轻松些。』王要对他们如此说：『我的小拇指头比我父亲的腰还粗。
verses.en: The young advisers with whom Rehoboam[NOTE:1] had grown up said to him, “Say this to these people who have said to you, ‘Your father made us work hard, but now lighten our burden.’[NOTE:2] Say this to them: ‘I am a lot harsher than my father![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Your father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter upon us.”

Heb “My little one is thicker than my father’s hips.” The referent of “my little one” is not clear. The traditional view is that it refers to the little finger. As the following statement makes clear, Rehoboam’s point is that he is more harsh and demanding than his father.

verses.zh: 我父亲使你们负重轭，我必使你们负更重的轭！我父亲用鞭子责打你们，我要用蝎子鞭责打你们！』」
verses.en: My father imposed heavy demands on you; I will make them even heavier.[NOTE:1] My father punished you with ordinary whips; I will punish you with whips that really sting your flesh.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and now my father placed upon you a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke.”

Heb “My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.” “Scorpions” might allude to some type of torture using poisonous insects, but more likely it refers to a type of whip that inflicts an especially biting, painful wound. Cf. CEV “whips with pieces of sharp metal.”

verses.zh: 耶罗波安和众百姓遵着罗波安王所说「你们第三日再来见我」的那话，第三日他们果然来了。
verses.en: Jeroboam and all the people reported[NOTE:1] to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had ordered when he said, “Return to me on the third day.”
notes: Heb “came.”

verses.zh: 王用严厉的话回答百姓，不用老年人给他所出的主意，
verses.en: The king responded to the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the older men

verses.zh: 照着少年人所出的主意对民说：「我父亲使你们负重轭，我必使你们负更重的轭！我父亲用鞭子责打你们，我要用蝎子鞭责打你们！」
verses.en: and followed[NOTE:1] the advice of the younger ones. He said, “My father imposed heavy demands on you; I will make them even heavier.[NOTE:2] My father punished you with ordinary whips; I will punish you with whips that really sting your flesh.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and spoke to them according to.”
Heb “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke.”
Heb “My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.” See the note on the same phrase in v. 11.

verses.zh: 王不肯依从百姓，这事乃出于耶和华，为要应验他藉示罗人亚希雅对尼八的儿子耶罗波安所说的话。
verses.en: The king refused to listen to the people, because the Lord was instigating this turn of events[NOTE:1] so that he might bring to pass the prophetic announcement he had made[NOTE:2] through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
notes: Heb “because this turn of events was from the Lord.”
Heb “so that he might bring to pass his word which the Lord spoke.”

verses.zh: 以色列众民见王不依从他们，就对王说：我们与大卫有甚么分儿呢？与耶西的儿子并没有关涉。以色列人哪，各回各家去吧！大卫家啊，自己顾自己吧！于是，以色列人都回自己家里去了，
verses.en: When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, the people answered the king, “We have no portion in David, no share in the son of Jesse![NOTE:1] Return to your homes, O Israel![NOTE:2] Now, look after your own dynasty, O David!”[NOTE:3] So Israel returned to their homes.[NOTE:4]
notes: We have no portion in David; no share in the son of Jesse. Their point seems to be that they have no familial relationship with David that brings them any benefits or places upon them any obligations. They are being treated like outsiders.
Heb “to your tents, Israel.” The word “return” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “Now see your house, David.”
Heb “went to their tents.”

verses.zh: 惟独住犹大城邑的以色列人，罗波安仍作他们的王。
verses.en: (Rehoboam continued to rule over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.)

verses.zh: 罗波安王差遣掌管服苦之人的亚多兰往以色列人那里去，以色列人就用石头打死他。罗波安王急忙上车，逃回耶路撒冷去了。
verses.en: King Rehoboam sent Adoniram,[NOTE:1] the supervisor of the work crews,[NOTE:2] out after them, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to jump into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.[NOTE:3]
notes: The MT has “Adoram” here, but the Old Greek translation and Syriac Peshitta have “Adoniram.” Cf. 1 Kgs 4:6.
The work crews. See the note on this expression in 4:6.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 这样，以色列人背叛大卫家，直到今日。
verses.en: So Israel has been in rebellion against the Davidic dynasty to this very day.

verses.zh: 以色列众人听见耶罗波安回来了，就打发人去请他到会众面前，立他作以色列众人的王。除了犹大支派以外，没有顺从大卫家的。
verses.en: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. No one except the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the Davidic dynasty.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “there was no one [following] after the house of David except the tribe of Judah, it alone.”

verses.zh: 罗波安来到耶路撒冷，招聚犹大全家和便雅悯支派的人共十八万，都是挑选的战士，要与以色列家争战，好将国夺回，再归所罗门的儿子罗波安。
verses.en: When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he summoned 180,000 skilled warriors from all Judah and the tribe of Benjamin[NOTE:1] to attack Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
notes: Heb “he summoned all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, 180,000 chosen men, accomplished in war.”

verses.zh: 但　神的话临到神人示玛雅，说：
verses.en: But God told Shemaiah the prophet,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying.”

verses.zh: 「你去告诉所罗门的儿子犹大王罗波安和犹大、便雅悯全家，并其余的民说：
verses.en: “Say this to King Rehoboam son of Solomon of Judah, and to all Judah and Benjamin, as well as the rest of the people,

verses.zh: 『耶和华如此说：你们不可上去与你们的弟兄以色列人争战。各归各家去吧！因为这事出于我。』」众人就听从耶和华的话，遵着耶和华的命回去了。
verses.en: ‘This is what the Lord has said: “Do not attack and make war with your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you go home. Indeed this thing has happened because of me.”’” So they obeyed the Lord’s message. They went home in keeping with the Lord’s message.

verses.zh: 耶罗波安在以法莲山地建筑示剑，就住在其中；又从示剑出去，建筑毗努伊勒。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Jeroboam built up Shechem in the Ephraimite hill country and lived there. From there he went out and built up Penuel.
notes: The Old Greek translation has here a lengthy section consisting of twenty-three verses that are not found in the MT.

verses.zh: 耶罗波安心里说：「恐怕这国仍归大卫家；
verses.en: Jeroboam then thought to himself:[NOTE:1] “Now the Davidic dynasty could regain the kingdom.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “said in his heart.”

Heb “Now the kingdom could return to the house of David.” The imperfect verbal form translated “could return” is understood as having a potential force here. Perhaps this is not strong enough; another option is “will return.”

verses.zh: 这民若上耶路撒冷去，在耶和华的殿里献祭，他们的心必归向他们的主―犹大王罗波安，就把我杀了，仍归犹大王罗波安。」
verses.en: If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] their loyalty could shift to their former master,[NOTE:2] King Rehoboam of Judah. They might kill me and return to King Rehoboam of Judah.”
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “the heart of these people could return to their master.”

verses.zh: 耶罗波安王就筹划定妥，铸造了两个金牛犊，对众民说：「以色列人哪，你们上耶路撒冷去实在是难；这就是领你们出埃及地的　神。」
verses.en: After the king had consulted with his advisers,[NOTE:1] he made two golden calves. Then he said to the people,[NOTE:2] “It is too much trouble for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look, Israel, here are your gods who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”
notes: The words “with his advisers” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “to them.”

verses.zh: 他就把牛犊一只安在伯特利，一只安在但。
verses.en: He put one in Bethel[NOTE:1] and the other in Dan.
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

verses.zh: 这事叫百姓陷在罪里，因为他们往但去拜那牛犊。
verses.en: This caused Israel to sin;[NOTE:1] the people went to Bethel and Dan to worship the calves.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and this thing became a sin.”

The MT reads “and the people went before the one to Dan.” It is likely that some words have been accidentally omitted and that the text originally said, “and the people went before the one at Bethel and before the one at Dan.”

verses.zh: 耶罗波安在邱坛那里建殿，将那不属利未人的凡民立为祭司。
verses.en: He built temples[NOTE:1] on the high places and appointed as priests common people who were not Levites.
notes: The Hebrew text has the singular, but the plural is preferable here (see 1 Kgs 13:32). The Old Greek translation and the Vulgate have the plural.

verses.zh: 耶罗波安定八月十五日为节期，像在犹大的节期一样，自己上坛献祭。他在伯特利也这样向他所铸的牛犊献祭，又将立为邱坛的祭司安置在伯特利。
verses.en: Jeroboam inaugurated a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month,[NOTE:1] like the festival celebrated in Judah.[NOTE:2] On the altar in Bethel he offered sacrifices to the calves he had made.[NOTE:3] In Bethel he also appointed priests for the high places he had made.
notes: The eighth month would correspond to October-November in modern reckoning.
The festival celebrated in Judah probably refers to the Feast of Tabernacles (i.e., Booths or Temporary Shelters), held in the seventh month (September-October). See also 1 Kgs 8:2.
Heb “and he offered up [sacrifices] on the altar; he did this in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves which he had made.”

verses.zh: 他在八月十五日，就是他私自所定的月日，为以色列人立作节期的日子，在伯特利上坛烧香。
verses.en: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month (a date he had arbitrarily chosen)[NOTE:1] Jeroboam[NOTE:2] offered sacrifices on the altar he had made in Bethel.[NOTE:3] He inaugurated a festival for the Israelites and went up to the altar to offer sacrifices.
notes: Heb “which he had chosen by himself.”
Heb “he”; the referent (Jeroboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
